contracts.protection_obligation: Merged from the two reviewer opinions (identical obligation, guard, and commit point): the @input_guardrail db_input_guardrail registered on db_agent must reject any user query submitted to POST /ask that is not a safe MongoDB READ query — i.e., a query containing destructive keywords (drop/delete/remove/truncate/update/insert), prompt-injection patterns, or any request to modify the database — by triggering its tripwire at agent-input time, so that Runner.run(db_agent, query) aborts before db_agent dispatches any MongoDB access tool.
scope_limits: The two reviewer opinions describe the same obligation, guard, and commit point and are merged into this single contract.

All eight tools registered on db_agent in the supplied source are read-only (find/find_one with limits and projections); no write-path tool exists in the supplied source, so this contract asserts a guard over agent tool execution, not an observed database mutation effect (stratum is tool_execution, not database).

The accept/reject classification is LLM-mediated via guardrail_agent; FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS and INJECTION_PATTERNS appear only inside guardrail_agent's instruction text — db_input_guardrail performs no deterministic keyword scan in the supplied source.

The handler's own resolve_db_name(data.db_url) call at line 402 (using MongoClient directly at lines 91-102) occurs before Runner.run and is not covered by the guardrail; the contract covers only the agent-run/tool-execution path.
Runtime effectiveness of the tripwire (that the agents SDK aborts Runner.run before tool dispatch when tripwire_triggered=true) is framework behavior not shown in the supplied file.
CORS configuration, API-key handling, and other generic validation in the handler are outside this contract's scope.
